page: Vultr voc-m-8c-64gb-400s-amd is an instance within the Optimized Cloud Compute family, configured with 8 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs derived from 4 physical AMD EPYC cores operating at 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, 32 MB L3 cache, and instruction support for AVX-512 vector extensions and cryptographic offloading. It provides 64.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation, and bundles 400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. No discrete graphics hardware is present.

Performance benchmarks highlight strong memory subsystem capability, with PassMark memory scoring in the top tier (3024.96) and uncached large block memory read speeds reaching 247.43 GB/sec. Single-core stress-ng throughput places in the top decile at 3434.87, complemented by single-threaded compression reaching 31.92 GB/sec. In contrast, multi-core CPU metrics sit within median bands, registering a PassMark CPU score of 22466.05, a multi-core stress-ng result of 27420.69, and a multi-core Geekbench rating of 8916.0.

Hardware tradeoffs manifest in larger machine-learning workloads, where 7B model prompt processing falls into the lower quartile at 25.19 tokens/sec. The configuration remains resource-dense for data-centric operations, providing dedicated thread scheduling without shared-core interference. Its balance of high memory density, sustained memory bandwidth, and local NVMe storage aligns technically with relational database engines, Redis caching clusters, search indexes, and concurrent data-processing services.
description: Vultr voc-m-8c-64gb-400s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance equipped with 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical AMD EPYC cores running at 2.0 GHz. The configuration includes 64.0 GB of RAM, a bundled 400 GB local NVMe SSD, and zero GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier memory test results alongside strong large-block memory read and write throughput. Single-core CPU compute performs in the upper deciles, whereas multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench outcomes place in the middle 50 percent range. The instance exhibits lower throughput on 7B parameter language model processing, establishing a profile better aligned with CPU-bound data operations than large AI workloads. With an 8 GB per vCPU density and dedicated hardware threads, this server serves memory-intensive operational workloads, including relational database engines, Redis key-value stores, and backend ETL tasks.
